polaris: For amorphous In2O3 and related transparent conducting oxides without long-range periodicity, is band-like transport sufficiently diagnosed by Anderson/Mott mobility-edge filling, or by a medium-range metal-s-orbital connectivity network plus O-O/coordination-defect thresholds?
framework: Network science plus graph-spectral robustness, repaired to avoid self-certification: structural coordinates define network metrics; validation observables must come from DFT/Wannier, experiment, or matched controls rather than only the same proxy Hamiltonian.
findings: Round 1 survives only after demotion from a proof to a measurement protocol. The sharp object is not 'graph Hamiltonian says graph matters'; it is whether structure-derived In-s connectivity metrics retain predictive power for independent Hall/Drude/Wannier observables at matched carrier density, matched EF-Ec, and matched onsite-disorder variance.
math_object: A weighted random geometric graph with motif-conditioned edges: V=In sites; E={(i,j): r_ij<r_cut and bridge criterion passes}; t_ij=t0*exp(-(r_ij-r0)/lambda)*(1+alpha_edge*I_edge+alpha_corner*I_corner)*exp(-beta*f_OO,ij). The repaired deeper object is a two-map factorization, structure X -> graph metrics M(X), and independent observable source Y -> transport/spectral labels; the claim needs M(X) to predict Y after non-network covariates are controlled.

lengths.r_ij: In-In distance, SI unit m; practical reporting in angstrom.
lengths.r0: reference In-In distance, same length unit as r_ij.
lengths.lambda: orbital-decay length, same length unit as r_ij and r0; in the toy ensemble lambda=0.55 angstrom, chosen as a tunable short-range decay scale, not an ab initio value.
lengths.r_cut: graph construction cutoff length; toy value r_cut=4.20 angstrom.

dimensionless_coefficients.alpha_edge: dimensionless multiplier for edge-sharing motifs; toy value +0.30.
dimensionless_coefficients.alpha_corner: dimensionless multiplier for corner-sharing motifs; toy value +0.10.
dimensionless_coefficients.beta: dimensionless defect penalty coefficient; beta>0 is required so larger f_OO weakens hopping; toy value beta=2.0.

distributions.P_r: P(r) is the normalized In-In pair-distance probability density: integral_0_infty P(r) dr = 1; unit 1/length, reported as angstrom^-1.
distributions.peak_area: A_[a,b]=integral_a^b P(r) dr; dimensionless probability mass in a shell. If computed from histogram counts, A_[a,b]=N_pairs(a<=r<b)/N_pairs(total).
distributions.edge_density_per_In: rho_E_atom = 2*E/N_In; dimensionless average edge count per In.
distributions.edge_density_per_volume: rho_E_vol = E/V_cell; unit length^-3, reported as angstrom^-3 for atomistic cells.

unit_and_normalization_repairs.threshold_direction: t_min is an energy threshold. Keeping only edges with abs(t_ij)>t_min means increasing t_min deletes weak edges, so S_GC, rho_E_atom, and z_eff cannot increase.

toy_generation_rules.cell: Cubic cell, side L=18.0 angstrom, periodic boundary conditions.
toy_generation_rules.base_In_positions: Generate blue-noise/random-sequential-addition In sites with minimum In-In distance 2.85 angstrom, then relax by 100 steps of pair repulsion to avoid unphysical overlap.
toy_generation_rules.O_positions: For each O, sample near the midpoint of a randomly chosen In-In pair with 3.0<r_InIn<4.4 angstrom, then add transverse Gaussian displacement sigma_O; reject O-In distances below 1.75 angstrom.
toy_generation_rules.ensemble_axis: Connectivity class is controlled by sigma_O and O-O defect injection: good(G) sigma_O=0.28 angstrom and f_OO_target=0.00; borderline(BD) sigma_O=0.45 angstrom and f_OO_target=0.04; bad(BA) sigma_O=0.65 angstrom and f_OO_target=0.10.
toy_generation_rules.defect_rule: An O-O defect motif is counted when an O-O distance is below d_OO_def=1.65 angstrom. Local f_OO,ij is the fraction of O-O defect motifs within 3.0 angstrom of the In_i-In_j edge midpoint.
toy_generation_rules.sharing_rule: An In-In pair is corner-sharing if exactly one O lies within 2.45 angstrom of both In atoms; edge-sharing if two or more shared O atoms pass this criterion.
toy_generation_rules.coordinate_output: If materialized, write XYZ files under D:/Claude/ai-reservations/LP29-AmorphousBands/current/B/inputs/toy_ensemble_v0/{G,BD,BA}_seedNN.xyz.

parameter_sources_or_calibration.r_cut: Initial r_cut=4.20 angstrom is the first minimum after the first In-In shell in the toy P(r). For real data, set r_cut to the first minimum of the normalized In-In P(r) for each ensemble family, then freeze it before model fitting.
parameter_sources_or_calibration.t_min: Toy t_min=0.35 eV for t0=1.0 eV. For real Wannier data, choose t_min by the knee in the empirical abs(t_ij) distribution or by cross-validated prediction of independent mobility/Drude labels, not by maximizing graph self-consistency.
parameter_sources_or_calibration.lambda: Toy lambda=0.55 angstrom. Real calibration: fit log(abs(t_ij/t0)) versus r_ij-r0 from DFT/Wannier hoppings at fixed motif class; lambda is the negative inverse slope length.
parameter_sources_or_calibration.beta: Toy beta=2.0 dimensionless. Real calibration: fit residual log hopping suppression after distance and sharing terms against local O-O defect fraction; constrain beta>0.
parameter_sources_or_calibration.alpha_edge_alpha_corner: Toy alpha_edge=0.30, alpha_corner=0.10 dimensionless. Real calibration: regress DFT/Wannier residual hoppings on motif indicators after distance correction.

non_self_certifying_validation_chain.principle: Graph metrics are explanatory variables only. At least one validation observable must be produced outside the same proxy graph Hamiltonian.
chain_A_preferred: Extract real amorphous coordinates from Nature Physics SI or reproduce AIMD snapshots following Aliano/Catellani/Cicero.
Independently run DFT/QSGW/Wannier on the same snapshots to obtain hoppings, spectral function/ridge linewidth, effective mass, and Drude weight.

Compare regression/classification models: Y_independent ~ M + carrier_density + EF_minus_Ec + onsite_variance + mstar + tau_proxy versus Y_independent ~ carrier_density + EF_minus_Ec + onsite_variance + mstar + tau_proxy.
Success requires out-of-sample improvement by M and correct sign under matched controls.
chain_B_experimental: Use same-family amorphous In2O3 or ITO films with measured Hall carrier density, Hall mobility, optical Drude weight, and processing/oxygen anneal metadata.
Obtain structural descriptors from PDF/EXAFS/fluctuation electron microscopy or atomistic models constrained by PDF.
Test whether structure-derived connectivity predicts residual mobility/Drude variance inside narrow carrier-density and EF-Ec bins.
chain_C_matched_control: For each toy or real structure, construct matched controls with same N_In, same P(r) peak area, same onsite disorder variance, and same carrier density label, but degree-preserving random rewiring or randomized O-O defect positions.

A valid network claim requires real motif-aware damage to outperform random/onsite-only controls in predicting independent labels. Proxy-Hamiltonian IPR on these controls is allowed only as a diagnostic, not as the sole validation.
non_self_certifying_validation_chain.explicit_cycle_break: The Round 1 graph Hamiltonian remains useful for mechanism sketches, but the Round 2 pass/fail test is external: Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral labels or matched-control residuals must not be generated by the same edge-weight formula that defines S_GC and z_eff.

alternative_explanations_and_controls.alternative: Carrier density and oxygen vacancy concentration drive mobility directly.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.control: Bin or match samples by Hall n within +/-10%; include O vacancy concentration or oxygen anneal condition as covariate; compare network residual effect inside bins.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.kill_condition_for_B: If network metrics lose predictive power after n/O-vacancy control, the graph threshold is not independent.

alternative_explanations_and_controls.alternative: Ordinary onsite disorder variance explains localization without edge topology.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.control: Compute sigma_epsilon from DFT site energies or structural proxies; compare edge-killing defects to onsite-only disorder at matched sigma_epsilon.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.kill_condition_for_B: If onsite variance alone predicts IPR/Drude/mu_H as well as motif-aware graph metrics, B collapses into standard Anderson disorder.

alternative_explanations_and_controls.alternative: Effective mass or scattering time differences dominate transport.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.control: Include m* from DFT/optical data and tau from Drude fits; test mobility residual mu_H/(e*tau/m*) or Drude weight residual after m* control.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.kill_condition_for_B: If m* or tau absorbs the network term, connectivity is a secondary correlate.

alternative_explanations_and_controls.control: Repeat N_In=64,128,256,512 toy or AIMD-derived ensembles; report S_GC and z_eff finite-size drift and confidence intervals.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.kill_condition_for_B: If threshold position drifts without convergence or disappears at larger N, the claimed transition is a small-cell artifact.

alternative_explanations_and_controls.alternative: EF-Ec definition or mobility-edge fitting error makes A look weak.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.control: Use a fixed EF-Ec extraction protocol across samples; include uncertainty propagation; compare models over the same EF-Ec posterior samples.
alternative_explanations_and_controls.kill_condition_for_B: If corrected EF-Ec predicts independent labels as well as or better than M(X), B is not a stronger sufficient criterion.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: At matched carrier density and matched EF-Ec, independently measured Hall mobility or optical Drude weight decreases with structure-derived z_eff and S_GC, with a sharper drop below S_GC about 0.6 in the toy-calibrated protocol.
falsifiable_predictions.observable: mu_H or Drude weight from experiment/DFT, not proxy graph Hamiltonian
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: Lower S_GC and z_eff -> lower mu_H and Drude weight after controls.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: O-O defects located on high-betweenness In-In bridges suppress independent Wannier hoppings/spectral ridge more than random O-O motifs at the same f_OO.
falsifiable_predictions.observable: Wannier abs(t_ij), spectral ridge linewidth, or matched-control residual
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: Targeted high-betweenness damage has stronger negative residual than random damage.

falsifiable_predictions.statement: Onsite-only disorder at matched variance should not reproduce the same mobility/Drude collapse unless it also reduces motif-aware connectivity.
falsifiable_predictions.observable: DFT/Wannier or experiment-constrained transport labels under matched sigma_epsilon
falsifiable_predictions.expected_direction: Edge/motif damage explains residual degradation beyond onsite variance.

strangest_prediction: The weird but testable claim is that two amorphous In2O3 samples can have indistinguishable carrier density, EF-Ec, and onsite disorder variance, yet differ in Hall/Drude response because one has O-O defects concentrated on high-betweenness In-s bridge edges. This is a targeted-attack phenomenon, not just disorder strength.

deepening_1.question: Does the isomorphism have a deeper mathematical structure after repair?
deepening_1.answer: Yes. The deeper layer is robustness under targeted attack in multiplex weighted geometric networks. Edge-sharing and corner-sharing are two coupled layers; O-O defects are not scalar noise but adversarial removal of bridge edges. The mobility edge becomes an emergent spectral boundary of a damaged multiplex network, but only if independent labels confirm it.

deepening_2.question: Does the borrowed network idea have a next-level extension in its home field?
deepening_2.answer: Yes. Network epidemiology distinguishes random failure from targeted immunization of hubs/bridges. Mapping back: equal f_OO can be harmless or fatal depending on whether defects hit high-betweenness In-s bridges. The next layer is not more average degree; it is edge vulnerability distribution V_e=betweenness_e*abs(t_e)/t0.

a_objection: A will say this is an overfitted structural proxy and that EF-Ec plus disorder variance already contains the physics. The repaired answer is operational: B wins only if M(X) improves independent Hall/Drude/Wannier/spectral prediction after matched n, EF-Ec, onsite variance, m*, tau, finite-size, and oxygen-vacancy controls. Otherwise B is demoted to a visualization of standard disorder physics.
failed_jumps: Pure graph-Hamiltonian validation was rejected because it self-certifies the edge formula.
Using only average degree was rejected because it cannot distinguish random edge loss from high-betweenness O-O bridge damage.
